about: Case study timeline data, written by scripts/build_case_study_timeline.py from data/case_studies.yaml; do not edit. Row keys: p study path, t title, k kind, s and e the period (YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD; e null while ongoing), cs and ce the core period when the study names one, y the year the study is placed under, sec sectors, cve CVE ids named in the study, act ATT&CK groups [id, name], tag tags, pdf and pptx download links, ev dated key events [date, label]. Rows are newest first.

CA-2003-21 announces the root compromise of the server behind GNU's primary FTP sites, reportedly from March
The Northeast blackout; the US-Canada task force later finds no evidence of a malicious cause
IN-2003-03: W32/Sobig.F
MS03-041 to MS03-045 published together, Microsoft's first monthly batch
Four Debian project machines compromised with a sniffed password and the do_brk() kernel flaw
CAN-SPAM approved (Pub. L. 108-187)

rows.t: The Year 2002 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: CA-2002-01: active exploitation of the CDE dtspcd overflow on Solaris, confirmed with Honeynet Project traces
CA-2002-03: SNMPv1 flaws across many vendors, found with the PROTOS c06-snmpv1 suite
Adrian Lamo gets into the New York Times internal network and its Op-Ed contributor database
IN-2002-04: the Spida worm spreads through null or weak sa passwords on SQL Server and MSDE
OpenSSH challenge-response advisory and CA-2002-18, five days after 3.3 turned on privilege separation
OpenSSH 3.4p1, 3.4 and 3.2.2p1 tarballs trojaned on the OpenBSD FTP server (30 or 31 July; CA-2002-24, 1 August)
CA-2002-27: the Apache/mod_ssl worm Slapper; thousands of systems, at least three variants
California SB 1386, the breach-notification law, approved by the Governor (operative 1 July 2003)
Trojaned Sendmail 8.12.6 tarballs appear on ftp.sendmail.org from about 28 September (CA-2002-28, 8 October)
Flood against all thirteen DNS root name servers, about 20:45 to 22:00 UTC
Trojaned tcpdump and libpcap on www.tcpdump.org, 11 to 13 November (CA-2002-30)
E-Government Act approved; Title III is the Federal Information Security Management Act

rows.t: United States-Attributed Threat Actors: The Public Record
ev: Earliest Regin sample timestamps
Stuxnet discovered
CrySyS publishes its Duqu analysis
Kaspersky discloses Flame
Kaspersky publishes its Regin analysis: 27 victims in 14 countries
Kaspersky discloses the Equation group
The Shadow Brokers post a sample archive they say came from Equation Group
Microsoft publishes MS17-010, fixing CVE-2017-0143 to CVE-2017-0148
WannaCry spreads with the EternalBlue exploit; NHS bodies in England are hit
The White House publishes the unclassified VEP charter
Kaspersky discloses Operation Triangulation; the FSB blames US intelligence the same day
China's Ministry of State Security alleges an NSA campaign against the National Time Service Center

rows.t: The Year 2001 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: IN-2001-01: the self-propagating ramen toolkit roots Linux hosts through wu-ftpd, rpc.statd and LPRng flaws
29 and 30 January: VeriSign issues two "Microsoft Corporation" code-signing certificates to an impostor
CA-2001-03: VBS/OnTheFly ("Anna Kournikova") mails itself through Outlook
CA-2001-11: the sadmind/IIS worm crosses from Solaris to IIS
MS01-033: the idq.dll overflow later used by Code Red, about four weeks before the worm
CAIDA: Code-Red v2 infects 359,104 hosts in under 14 hours
CA-2001-26: Nimda spreads by five paths, including the back doors earlier worms left
Seattle jury convicts Vasiliy Gorshkov on 20 counts
USA PATRIOT Act amends the computer fraud and surveillance statutes
Vitek Boden sentenced over the Maroochy Shire sewerage intrusion (ATT&CK campaign C0020)
Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime done at Budapest
MS01-059 and CA-2001-37: UPnP overflow leaves Windows XP vulnerable in its default configuration

rows.t: The Year 2000 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: CA-2000-01: Stacheldraht DDoS agents found on multiple compromised hosts
The President announces the national plan to defend America's cyberspace
Yahoo unreachable for about three hours; Amazon.com, eBay, Buy.com and CNN hit the next day (press reports)
Maroochy Shire: Boden alters pumping-station data from 9 February to 23 April (ATT&CK campaign C0020)
RCMP arrests 'mafia boy' in Montreal over the attack on CNN's site
Love Letter: first reported in Asia; CERT/CC advisory CA-2000-04 that night
CA-2000-13: wu-ftpd site exec format string flaw exploited for remote root
Carnivore widely reported, per EPIC; EPIC files a FOIA request the next day
IN-2000-10: automated exploitation of rpc.statd and wu-ftpd, hundreds of hosts in single incidents
NIST announces Rijndael as the proposed Advanced Encryption Standard
Government Information Security Reform Act enacted in Pub. L. 106-398
Gorshkov and Ivanov arrested in Seattle after a recorded meeting with the FBI's undercover company

rows.t: E-Commerce Threats: The Public Record, 1999 to 2026
ev: CD Universe extortion, 25 Dec 1999 to 9 Jan 2000: about 300,000 card numbers claimed, card data posted after refusal (Reported)
TJX finds suspicious software; it determines on 27 Dec that customer data was stolen and announces the intrusion on 17 Jan 2007
DOJ charges eleven defendants, including Albert Gonzalez, over nine retailers and more than 40 million card numbers
Cards used in Target's US stores exposed, 27 Nov to 18 Dec 2013; about 40 million card accounts
US-CERT TA14-212A on Backoff point-of-sale malware
British Airways' modified JavaScript copies card data to an attacker domain, 21 Aug to 5 Sep 2018
ICO fines British Airways GBP 20m, down from GBP 183.39m proposed
First CosmicSting (CVE-2024-34102) attacks in the wild, twelve days after Adobe's fix (Reported)
polyfill.io serves malicious code; Cloudflare rewrites links to its mirror, 25 to 26 Jun 2024
PCI DSS 6.4.3 and 11.6.1 on payment page scripts become required
SessionReaper (CVE-2025-54236) attacks begin (Reported); KEV entry on 24 Oct
PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356) added to KEV

rows.t: The Year 1999 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: DES Challenge III: distributed.net and the EFF DES Cracker find the key in 22 hours 15 minutes
CA-1999-01: trojaned TCP Wrappers 7.6 source on a number of FTP servers
Deputy Secretary of Defense Hamre tells Congress DoD detects 80 to 100 events a day
CA-1999-04: Melissa, a Word macro virus spreading by email; over 100,000 computers by 29 March
IN-99-03: CIH can erase the hard drive and overwrite the system BIOS
CA-1999-06: ExploreZip zeroes Office and source-code files and spreads to shares
IN-99-04: scripted attacks chain the cmsd, statd/automountd and ToolTalk flaws
Kevin Mitnick sentenced to 46 months
The CVE List launches publicly with 321 records
Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act puts a security and confidentiality obligation on financial institutions
IN-99-07: trinoo and Tribe Flood Network installed on hosts taken through RPC flaws
CA-1999-17: Tribe FloodNet 2K, with spoofed sources and MacOS 9 amplification

rows.t: The Year 1998 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: CA-1998-01: continuing smurf floods through IP broadcast addresses congest or knock out NSPs, ISPs and other sites
Solar Sunrise: attacks on Air Force, Navy and Marine Corps unclassified systems (1 to 26 February) (Reported)
Attorney General Reno unveils the National Infrastructure Protection Center
DOJ announces an arrest in Israel and searches of two California teenagers' homes; no sign of a state-sponsored campaign
IN-98.01: TCP port 1 sweeps for IRIX hosts and automated logins to default accounts with no passwords
PDD-63, Critical Infrastructure Protection, and PDD-62 on unconventional threats to the homeland
CA-1998-07 and MS98-002: Bleichenbacher's PKCS #1 attack can recover information from SSL sessions
IN-98.03: a compromised host holds 186,126 accounts with encrypted passwords, 47,642 already cracked
Back Orifice released at DEF CON VI; MS98-010 follows on 4 August
CA-1998-12: NFS mountd overflow, mainly on Linux, actively exploited with large-scale scanning
Digital Millennium Copyright Act, Pub. L. 105-304
IN-98-06: scripted tools scan the portmapper, exploit mountd on Linux and add a passwordless privileged account

rows.t: The Year 1997 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: Office 97 reaches North American shops with VBA5 in every application
CA-97.05: sendmail 8.8.3 and 8.8.4 MIME conversion overflow, exploitable despite firewalls
CA-97.08: INN runs attacker commands from crafted control messages
CA-97.09: IMAP and POP login overflow gives remote root; large-scale automated scans all year
Card data on more than 100,000 accounts sold to undercover FBI agents; arrest at San Francisco Airport (Reported)
Eligible Receiver 97: Joint Chiefs of Staff J-5 tasking for the exercise scenario
Reno v. ACLU: the Communications Decency Act's indecency provisions struck down
CA-97.22: BIND cache poisoning now being exploited
Phrack 51 publishes The Art of Port Scanning, introducing nmap
PCCIP issues Critical Foundations: Protecting America's Infrastructures
CA-97.25: sanitizing user-supplied data in CGI scripts
CA-97.28 Teardrop and Land; the No Electronic Theft Act becomes law

rows.t: The Year 1996 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: CA-96.01: UDP packet storms between chargen and echo, typically with IP spoofing
CA-96.06: the phf example CGI program in NCSA httpd and Apache is actively exploited
Justice Department charges the Harvard intruder after the first court-ordered wiretap on a computer network
GAO/AIMD-96-84: as many as 250,000 attacks on Defense systems in 1995, about 4 percent of test attacks detected
Executive Order 13010 creates the President's Commission on Critical Infrastructure Protection
Omega Engineering: an insider's time bomb deletes the company's manufacturing programs
Justice Department web site altered and shut down (16 or 17 August)
CA-96.21: TCP SYN flooding and IP spoofing, with no complete solution yet
Pub. L. 104-294: the Economic Espionage Act and the National Information Infrastructure Protection Act
Phrack 49 publishes Aleph One's Smashing The Stack For Fun And Profit
A SYN flood takes more than 3,000 sites hosted by WebCom off the air for 40 hours
CA-96.26: oversized ping packets crash, freeze or reboot systems

rows.t: The Year 1995 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: CA-95:01: forged source addresses beat address-based trust; a kernel tool hijacks open terminal and login sessions
FBI and the Raleigh-Durham Fugitive Task Force arrest Kevin Mitnick after a two-week electronic manhunt
BSI publishes BS 7799-1:1995, an information security management code of practice
SATAN released; CIAC bulletin F-20 records the release and announces the Courtney detector
CERT heads-up: 170 IP spoofing attacks in a few weeks, at least 80 against name servers, routers and network systems
Tatu Ylonen announces SSH 1.0 as a replacement for rlogin, rsh and rcp
Navy NCCOSC detects an intrusion traced to Harvard's FAS host (late August)
Export-grade 40-bit SSL challenge broken by brute force
Virus Bulletin analyses Winword.Concept, the first Word macro virus seen spreading
Netscape Bugs Bounty: $1,000 to the first finder of a major security bug in its browser beta (Reported)
CA-95:18 Widespread Attacks: hundreds of sites hit through automated scanning of already-advised flaws
Argentine authorities seize the Harvard intruder's equipment in Buenos Aires

rows.t: The Dot-Com Era: Cyber Events, 1994 to 2003
ev: Vladimir Levin and confederates begin transferring about $10 million from Citibank subsidiaries (Reported)
Moonlight Maze intrusions begin against mainly US military, research and university networks
Solar Sunrise, 1 to 26 Feb 1998: attacks on unclassified DoD networks, at least eleven (Reported)
Seven L0pht members and Peter G. Neumann testify to the Senate Committee on Governmental Affairs
Melissa reports begin; CERT/CC advisory CA-1999-04 follows on 27 March
CVE List launches publicly with 321 records and a 19-member Editorial Board
Yahoo unreachable for about three hours after a DDoS; Amazon, eBay, Buy.com and CNN hit on 8 Feb (Reported)
CERT/CC CA-2000-04 on the Love Letter worm; over 500,000 affected systems reported by 8 May
Code Red v2 begins about 10:00 UTC and infects 359,104 hosts in under fourteen hours (CAIDA)
Council of Europe Convention on Cybercrime done at Budapest
Slammer begins slightly before 05:30 UTC; over 90 percent of vulnerable hosts within ten minutes
CERT/CC CA-2003-20 on W32/Blaster, 26 days after Microsoft's MS03-026

rows.t: The Year 1994 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: CA-94:01: sniffers on compromised hosts have captured access information for tens of thousands of systems
FIPS 185, the Escrowed Encryption Standard (Clipper), approved and published
FBI arrests CIA officer Aldrich Ames in Arlington, Virginia
CA-94:05 publishes MD5 checksums for SunOS files after intruders build Trojans to match the sum checksum
Rome Laboratory first penetrated, per audit logs; staff find a sniffer on 28 March
CA-94:07: intruder-modified wuarchive ftpd 2.2 and 2.1f source carries a root back door
New Scotland Yard arrests the 16-year-old Datastream Cowboy; the US record never identifies Kuji
About 40 illegal transfers totalling more than $10 million from a US bank's cash management system begin (to October)
Pub. L. 103-322 amends 18 U.S.C. 1030 and adds a civil action
CA-94:14: Trojaned ircII 2.2.9 source, on FTP sites since May, is actively exploited
US Naval Academy penetrated from three countries and two US universities; more than 12,000 passwords changed
IP spoofing attack on Tsutomu Shimomura's systems begins

rows.t: The Year 1993 in Intrusions: A Dated Record
ev: CA-93:03: SunOS default file permissions give local root; CERT sees an increasing number of attackers exploiting them
Steve Jackson Games v. US Secret Service decided: Privacy Protection Act and Stored Communications Act violated
Paul Bedworth acquitted at Southwark Crown Court after a four-week Computer Misuse Act trial
White House announces the voluntary Clipper Chip key-escrow initiative
Channel Videodat broadcasts a Tremor-infected PKUNZIP to a claimed 60,000 subscribers
CA-93:10 Anonymous FTP Activity: compromise, disk-filling denial of service, trading of pirated software
Senate hearing "Auditing the Auditors": IRS staff browsing taxpayer records
The Air Force Electronic Warfare Center is redesignated the Air Force Information Warfare Center
CA-93:14: the Internet Security Scanner is posted to comp.sources.misc; CERT expects malicious use
CA-93:15: the Sun sendmail flaw is being actively exploited
Mark Abene (Phiber Optik) sentenced to a year and a day in federal court in Manhattan
The seclists.org Bugtraq archive opens with a thread on CA-93:17

rows.t: Kevin Mitnick: Ghost in the Wires and The Art of Intrusion
ev: Guilty plea to possessing 16 unauthorized MCI codes and computer fraud for copying a DEC security program (Reported)
Fugitive intrusion series against technology companies begins, after a warrant for violating the 1989 supervised release
IP-spoofing and session-hijack intrusion on Shimomura's systems; his account names no attacker
Shimomura posts the technical details of the Christmas Day attack to Usenet
Mitnick arrested in North Carolina
Ninth Circuit upholds the sentence and the bar on computers and cellular phones during supervised release
Global plea: four counts of wire fraud, two of computer fraud, one of intercepting a wire communication
Sentenced to 46 months, 68 months combined, with restitution of just over $4,125
Released; supervised release runs to 20 January 2003
Testifies to the Senate Committee on Governmental Affairs on pretext calls and weak callbacks
CISA and FBI publish AA23-320A on Scattered Spider's help desk impersonation
HHS HC3 analyst note on social engineering of health sector IT help desks

rows.t: Five Hacks and Why They Worked: The Cases in Fancy Bear Goes Phishing
ev: The Morris worm is released from an MIT computer at about 8:30 p.m. and spreads through sendmail, fingerd, trusted hosts and guessed passwords
The Dark Avenger releases his first virus from Sofia, begun in September 1988
The judgment against Morris sets three years probation, 400 hours of community service and a $10,050 fine
The Dark Avenger's Mutation Engine (MtE) lets any virus mutate through one subroutine
A Massachusetts juvenile is sentenced to 11 months for entry to an ISP and a telephone provider, accounts at an identity-data company and a denial of service
GRU Unit 26165 phishes the Clinton campaign chairman with a spoofed Google notice; over 50,000 emails taken
The DNC announces the Russian intrusion; CrowdStrike names two actors, APT29 and APT28
Over 20,000 DNC emails and documents released, about three days before the convention
Mirai hits Krebs on Security with a 623 Gbps attack
The Dyn attack, which the USENIX paper attributes to Mirai cluster 6, not the original cluster 1
Informations and plea agreements against three Mirai and clickfraud defendants filed in Alaska
Twelve GRU officers indicted in the District of Columbia over the 2016 intrusions and leaks

rows.t: The Cuckoo's Egg Intrusion: Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory, 1986
ev: At least five diskettes handed over in East Berlin from May to November 1986 (DER SPIEGEL, Reported)
LBL's accounting program fails to balance: a new account with no billing address
US request for help reaches the Deutsche Bundespost (DER SPIEGEL, Reported)
Alarmed SDI bait files hold the intruder for more than an hour while the trace to West Germany completes
Stoll's "Stalking the Wily Hacker" published in Communications of the ACM
Internet worm released; Stoll posts one of the first public warnings on RISKS
CERT/CC established by DARPA at the SEI, Carnegie Mellon
Three arrests after house searches; the Interior Ministry confirms the suspects supplied the KGB (Reported)
Three hackers indicted on espionage charges (AP, Reported)
Stoll posts the details of his book The Cuckoo's Egg (Doubleday, 1989)
Court in Celle gives Carl, Hess and Brzezinski suspended sentences (Reported)
RFC 1244 frames "Protect and Proceed" against "Pursue and Prosecute" and cites both Stoll works

rows.t: Cybercrime and Hacktivism in Four Books: Kingpin, Fatal System Error, We Are Anonymous, The Hacker Crackdown
ev: AT&T long-distance crash from its own 4ESS software update, at first suspected to be hackers
Secret Service searches Steve Jackson Games and seizes the Illuminati BBS
Operation Sundevil, 7 to 8 May 1990: about 27 warrants, 150 agents, 13 cities
Neidorf trial, 23 to 27 July 1990: the prosecution moves to dismiss and a mistrial is declared (Reported)
Fifth Circuit affirms Steve Jackson Games: seizing stored unread e-mail is not an intercept
Shadowcrew indictment and Operation Firewall's 28 arrests announced
Russian court sentences three bookmaker DDoS extortionists to eight years each (Reported)
Max Butler sentenced to 13 years and $27.5 million restitution
HBGary Federal breach: SQL injection, cracked and reused passwords, hijacked mail
FBI approaches Monsegur, who agrees to cooperate that night (about this date)
Jeremy Hammond sentenced to 10 years for computer hacking conspiracy
Monsegur sentenced to time served

rows.t: Before the Internet: Computer Threats, 1960 to 1990
ev: Bell System Technical Journal publishes Breen and Dahlbom on in-band trunk signaling
Ware report for the Defense Science Board: threat taxonomy, trap doors, insider infiltration
Anderson report: penetration is easy, the Trojan horse defined, the reference monitor introduced
GAO FGMSD-76-27: 69 federal cases, mostly by users with limited technical knowledge
Fred Cohen's first experimental virus, conceived 3 Nov and demonstrated 10 Nov 1983
Pub. L. 98-473 creates 18 U.S.C. 1030
Pub. L. 99-474, the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act of 1986
First known CHRISTMA EXEC infection, 9 to 14 Dec 1987 on BITNET and IBM's VNET
Morris worm released from an MIT computer
CERT/CC established by DARPA at the SEI; first advisory CA-1988-01
AIDS Information disks posted from London, 8 to 12 Dec 1989
UK Computer Misuse Act 1990 receives Royal Assent
